learn.title: Rooftop Solar and Net Metering in India
learn.intro: Rooftop solar empowers homeowners to become active producers rather than just consumers. By installing panels on your roof, you contribute to India's massive renewable energy goals while lowering your electricity bills. Net metering is the crucial policy mechanism that makes this economically viable for millions of households across the country.
learn.c1_text: Think of your roof as a mini power plant. Solar panels capture sunlight and convert it into DC electricity. It is like a garden that grows energy instead of vegetables, providing you with a constant harvest of clean, renewable power every single day.
learn.c2_text: When your panels produce more energy than you use, the excess flows back to the grid. A net meter tracks this exchange. You essentially 'deposit' energy into the grid like a bank account, earning credits to offset your usage during the night.
learn.c3_text: The MNRE promotes rooftop solar through various subsidies and schemes. In India, net metering allows consumers to reduce their electricity bills significantly by selling surplus power back to the local DISCOM, fostering a decentralized and resilient national energy grid.
learn.stat1: India: Massive rooftop solar push via MNRE
learn.stat2: Net metering: Credit for excess power

learn.title: How Solar PV Works: The Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: Understanding the physics of solar panels reveals the magic of the photoelectric effect. This fundamental scientific principle is the backbone of the global energy transition, allowing us to harvest the most abundant energy source in our solar system to power our modern digital lives.
learn.c1_text: Imagine sunlight as a stream of tiny energetic ping-pong balls called photons. When these photons strike a solar cell, they knock electrons loose from their atoms. It is like a game of billiards where the white ball (photon) hits the colored balls (electrons).
learn.c2_text: The solar cell is designed with an internal electric field that forces these loose electrons to move in one direction. This flow of electrons is what we call electricity. It turns light directly into a usable direct current (DC) stream.
learn.c3_text: This technology is driving the global shift away from fossil fuels. By utilizing the photoelectric effect, solar PV can be scaled from tiny calculators to massive utility-scale farms that provide megawatts of clean energy to entire cities worldwide.
learn.stat1: Solar PV: Most abundant energy source
learn.stat2: Direct conversion of light to DC

learn.title: Small Wind Turbines for Homes and Communities
learn.intro: Small wind turbines offer a localized solution for renewable energy, especially in windy, rural, or coastal areas. They provide a way for communities to harvest kinetic energy from the wind, reducing reliance on centralized fossil fuel power plants and enhancing energy independence.
learn.c1_text: As wind blows past the turbine blades, it creates lift, similar to how an airplane wing works. This force turns the rotor, which is connected to a generator. It is like a high-tech windmill that turns motion into usable electricity.
learn.c2_text: The rotating shaft spins magnets inside coils of wire within the generator. This movement creates an electromagnetic field that induces an electrical current. This process converts the kinetic energy of the wind into the electrical energy used in homes.
learn.c3_text: Small wind is vital for remote communities or microgrids. In many regions, combining small wind with solar provides a more stable power supply, as wind often blows stronger at night or during stormy weather when solar is unavailable.
learn.stat1: Small wind: Ideal for rural areas

learn.title: Green Hydrogen: PEM vs. Alkaline Electrolysis
learn.intro: Green hydrogen is the 'Swiss Army Knife' of the energy transition. By using renewable electricity to split water, we create a carbon-free fuel that can decarbonize heavy industries and long-haul transport, serving as a critical storage medium for excess renewable energy.
learn.c1_text: Electrolysis uses electricity to split water (H2O) into hydrogen and oxygen. Think of it like using a wedge to split a log; the electricity acts as the force that separates the hydrogen molecules from the oxygen atoms.
learn.c2_text: Alkaline electrolysis uses a liquid electrolyte and is a mature, low-cost technology. PEM (Proton Exchange Membrane) uses a solid polymer electrolyte; it is more expensive but can respond much faster to the fluctuating nature of wind and solar power.
learn.c3_text: As global capacity increases, green hydrogen will become essential for sectors that cannot easily run on batteries. It bridges the gap between intermittent renewable generation and the constant energy demands of heavy industry and heavy-duty transport.

learn.title: Bifacial Solar Panels: Double-Sided Power
learn.intro: Bifacial solar panels represent a significant leap in efficiency for solar installations. By capturing light from both sides, they maximize energy yield per square meter, making solar projects more economically attractive and reducing the land footprint required for large-scale energy production.
learn.c1_text: Standard panels only catch light from the top. Bifacial panels use transparent backsheets to catch sunlight hitting the rear side. It is like having a window that catches light from both the front and the reflection from the ground.
learn.c2_text: The extra power comes from 'albedo'—the light reflected off the ground. Surfaces like white gravel, sand, or snow reflect much more light than dark soil, significantly increasing the total energy output of the bifacial modules.
learn.c3_text: For large-scale solar farms, bifacial technology can increase total energy yield by 10% to 30% depending on the ground reflectivity. This makes solar more competitive against fossil fuels by squeezing more value out of every installed panel.

learn.title: Green Ammonia: The Future of Clean Shipping
learn.intro: Ammonia (NH3) is a versatile molecule that is key to a zero-carbon future. When produced using green hydrogen, it becomes a powerful carrier for renewable energy, capable of decarbonizing the massive shipping industry and the global fertilizer market.
learn.c1_text: Green ammonia is made by combining green hydrogen with nitrogen from the air. Think of it as a chemical 'container' that holds renewable energy in a stable, liquid form that is much easier to transport than gas.
learn.c2_text: Traditional shipping uses heavy fuel oils that emit massive amounts of CO2. Ammonia can be burned in modified engines with virtually zero carbon emissions, making it a game-changer for the massive global maritime logistics network.
learn.c3_text: Beyond fuel, green ammonia is essential for carbon-free fertilizers. Transitioning from fossil-fuel-based to green ammonia production will drastically reduce the carbon footprint of global food production and the agricultural supply chain.
